clue.text: PM and a baker initially studied unleavened food

parts.note: William Pitt (elder or younger) was a British Prime Minister

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word baker

parts.note: first letter of baker
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A prime minister and a baker have looked into flatbreads.
explanation.walkthrough: PM stands for Prime Minister here: Pitt the Elder and Pitt the Younger both held the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread made with little or no rising, so it counts as unleavened.

clue.text: Picture from one publication in English

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a mag is a magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: A caption crediting a photo taken from an English magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to see it in the mind's eye, which is to conjure it up mentally.

clue.text: Instruct famous archer

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate meanings: a verb for giving orders and the legendary Swiss crossbowman.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone what to do is to order them; William Tell is the legendary marksman of Swiss folklore.

clue.text: Cricketer leaving middle a hero

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket 'the middle' is the pitch itself, so the surface reads as a batsman walking off; in the wordplay it is the centre letter S that leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Batman is the caped comic-book crime-fighter, a classic superhero of DC Comics.

clue.text: Adore old ruined city that's fabulously rich

explanation.surface: Someone adores an old ruined city that was once fabulously wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado is the legendary South American city of gold sought by Spanish conquistadors; fabulously means in fable as well as extremely.

clue.text: Some Sudanese people found in Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A few Sudanese people have settled in Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: Danes are the inhabitants of Denmark, one of the Scandinavian countries.

clue.text: Father and uncle finally phone for VIP transport

a mobile is a mobile phone

explanation.walkthrough: Father is also the title of a priest, which suits the answer, but here it is simply pop.
explanation.definitionFit: The popemobile is the specially built vehicle that carries the pontiff, a very important person, among crowds.

clue.text: Small vehicle to rent out is red

explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright shade of red.

clue.text: Teach group of swimmers

clue.text: Bowler, perhaps, might ultimately strain to get this?

definitions.text: Bowler, perhaps, might ultimately strain to get this?

parts.note: a bowler is a kind of hat

parts.note: last letter of might

clue.text: Pursues one of two options

lasses are girls or young women
